llm.asm

 Three complete LLM projects written in 100% pure x86-64 NASM assembly. 
Zero C, zero C++, zero Rust, zero libc, zero libm, zero runtime dependencies.

Assembled directly with nasm and linked with ld . Every math kernel ( expf , sincosf , RMSNorm , RoPE , SiLU , Softmax ), AVX2+FMA+F16C GEMM/GEMV engine, BPE tokenizer, clone() / futex() thread pool, bare-metal SMP kernel, analytical backward pass, AdamW optimizer, and live Unicode Braille TUI is hand-written x86-64 assembly ( 17,252 lines total across all three projects).

 The Trilogy

 Project Binary Size Deps Key Numbers 
 --- --- ---: ---: --- 
 01-qwen3-inference/ build/asm-llm 14,712 B (14,008 B FAST Q8=0 ) 0 Static Linux ELF running Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (Q8 0, built-in BPE tokenizer, GQA + QK-Norm + RoPE + SwiGLU, single-shot & --chat multi-turn KV-cache REPL). FAST Q8=1 (default): 126.8 tok/s decode at 40T ( 20.7 tok/s at 1T), +18% to +36% faster than llama.cpp CPU ( Q8 0 ) across 1..40T , 0.99965 cosine & 64/64 exact greedy tokens vs PyTorch FP32. 
 02-baremetal-os/ build/asm-llm-os.elf 24,252 B (23,612 B FAST Q8=0 ) 0 Bootable bare-metal Qwen3-0.6B OS with no Linux or Windows. Multiboot 1 - Long Mode - AVX2/FMA/F16C - ACPI/APIC SMP - VGA + PS/2 + COM1 multi-turn KV-cache chat ( /clear , /think , /bench ). 74–94 ms boot, 134.9 tok/s KVM EPYC ( 23.7 tok/s 1 vCPU, 136.6 tok/s peak), 55.4 tok/s live on Proxmox Xeon E5-2670 v3 with 0 GB disk. 
 03-minigpt-train/ build/asm-gpt-train 32,944 B 0 From-scratch FP32 Mini-GPT trainer and sampler. Register-blocked 6x16 AVX2+FMA SGEMM, full analytical backward pass ( 1.0000000000 cosine across all 21 gradient tensors vs PyTorch CPU), decoupled AdamW, 27,662 train tok/s , live 80x24 Braille TUI, val loss 4.19 - 1.51 on TinyShakespeare in 4 min. 

---

 Head-to-Head CPU Decode Benchmark: llm.asm vs llama.cpp ( Qwen3-0.6B Q8 0 )

Measured on the same machine ( AMD EPYC 7642 , 47C online, 256 MiB L3, DDR4, CPU-only -ngl 0 ), same model ( Qwen3-0.6B Q8 0 : 613.66 MiB .asmbin v2 FP16-scale vs 604.15 MiB GGUF Q8 0 ), 34 prompt tokens / 64 generated tokens, 3 -run average:

 Threads llm.asm ( FAST Q8=0 , FP32 act) llama.cpp ( Q8 0 , -ngl 0 ) llm.asm ( FAST Q8=1 , 14.7 KB) vs llama.cpp Bare-Metal OS KVM ( FAST Q8=1 ) 
 ---: ---: ---: ---: ---: ---: 
 1 7.18 tok/s 16.63 tok/s 20.70 tok/s 1.24x (+24.5%) 23.67 tok/s 
 4 28.12 tok/s 51.08 tok/s 69.24 tok/s 1.36x (+35.6%) 78.89 tok/s 
 8 53.09 tok/s 80.79 tok/s 103.64 tok/s 1.28x (+28.3%) 118.08 tok/s 
 16 77.50 tok/s 103.03 tok/s 121.86 tok/s 1.18x (+18.3%) 134.94 tok/s 
 24 91.88 tok/s 104.11 tok/s 123.72 tok/s 1.19x (+18.8%) 132.90 tok/s 
 32 96.63 tok/s 103.82 tok/s 122.51 tok/s 1.18x (+18.0%) 133.75 tok/s 
 40 98.50 tok/s 105.08 tok/s 125.86 tok/s (peak 126.81) 1.20x (+19.8%) — 

 (Note: llama.cpp uses batched GEMM for prompt prefill pp34 , whereas llm.asm runs token-by-token GEMV. For autoregressive decode tg64 , llm.asm ( FAST Q8=1 ) combines INT8xINT8 AVX2 vpmaddubsw / vpmaddwd , .asmbin v2 FP16 block scales ( F16C vcvtph2ps ), monotonic next-row prefetch, contiguous head-major KV-cache, and parallel GQA attention — beating llama.cpp by +18%..+36% across 1..40 threads while producing bit-exact deterministic outputs across all thread counts. The bare-metal OS gains another 10% from 2 MiB huge-page identity mapping.) 

---

 Live Output & Visual Proof

 Phase 2: Booting Qwen3-0.6B Directly on Bare Metal (QEMU KVM, 16 vCPUs)

 

 Phase 2: Running Live on a Proxmox VE VM (0 GB Disk, Intel Xeon E5-2670 v3, 12 Cores)

 

 Phase 3: Pure-Assembly Live 80x24 UTF-8 Braille TUI ( build/asm-gpt-train )

 

---

 Quick Start

Clone the repo and build everything with make all :

 

 1. Run Qwen3-0.6B Inference in 14 KB ( 01-qwen3-inference/ )

 

Full step-by-step setup, model download, CLI flags, and benchmarks: 01-qwen3-inference/README.md .

 2. Boot Bare-Metal Qwen3-0.6B OS in 24 KB ( 02-baremetal-os/ )

 

Full QEMU KVM, bootable ISO, and 0 GB disk Proxmox VE deployment guide: 02-baremetal-os/README.md .

 3. Train Mini-GPT from Scratch in 32 KB ( 03-minigpt-train/ )

Zero Python required to train or run inference:

 

Full training, live Braille TUI, checkpoint chat loop, and PyTorch gradient check guide: 03-minigpt-train/README.md .

---

 Repository Layout

 

---

 System Requirements

- CPU: x86-64 with AVX2 + FMA + F16C (Intel Haswell / AMD Excavator or newer).
- Build tools: nasm and GNU binutils ( ld , objcopy ).
 
- Phase 1 & 3 runtime: Any Linux x86-64 kernel. Zero shared libraries ( readelf -d reports no dynamic section).
- Phase 2 runtime (optional): qemu-system-x86 64 with KVM, or any x86-64 hypervisor/bare-metal machine (Proxmox VE, VirtualBox, real hardware). Building bootable ISOs uses grub-mkrescue ( grub-pc-bin , grub-efi-amd64-bin , mtools , xorriso ).
- Offline tooling (optional): python3 + numpy only for one-time Qwen3-0.6B .asmbin export and reference verification ( torch + transformers only if running PyTorch parity checks).

---

 Architecture & Verification Summary

Every phase is built on the same engineering rules: no runtime libraries, deterministic parallel partitioning, and numerical verification against independent Python/PyTorch references.

- Shared assembly core ( shared/ ): Phase 2 compiles the exact same math.asm , matmul.asm , tokenizer.asm , and transformer.asm with -DBARE METAL (swapping Linux mmap / clone / write for physical Multiboot modules, APIC spin-barriers, and VGA+COM1 drivers). Phase 3 reuses syscalls.asm and math.asm .
- Phase 1 verification: All math/SIMD kernels pass unit tests within 1e-7..1e-6 ( init rope freqs FP64 < 5e-14 ) for both FAST Q8=1 and FAST Q8=0 across v1 FP32 and v2 FP16 scale formats. FAST Q8=1 matches PyTorch FP32 Qwen3-0.6B with cosine = 0.9996517 and 64/64 exact greedy tokens ( FAST Q8=0 matches the Python Q8 0 reference with cosine = 1.000000000 ). Bit-exact deterministic from 1T to 40T .
- Phase 2 verification: 100% token-exact and byte-for-byte identical to Phase 1 across 5 test

install.title: Quick Start
install.html:
Clone the repo and build everything with make all:

git clone https://github.com/alesha-pro/llm.asm.git
cd llm.asm
make all
1. Run Qwen3-0.6B Inference in 14 KB (01-qwen3-inference/)
# Export compact .asmbin v2 (FP16 block scales, 613.66 MiB; or --scale-dtype fp32 for legacy v1)
python3 scripts/export_weights.py --model-dir models/qwen3-0.6b-bf16 --out models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin --scale-dtype fp16
# Build with FAST_Q8=1 (default: INT8xINT8 AVX2 + parallel GQA) or FAST_Q8=0 (exact FP32 activations)
make inference FAST_Q8=1
./build/asm-llm -m models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin -p "Explain how a CPU cache works in 3 concise sentences." -n 128 -t 16
# Or start an interactive multi-turn chat preserving the KV-cache across turns:
./build/asm-llm -m models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin --chat -t 16

Full step-by-step setup, model download, CLI flags, and benchmarks: 01-qwen3-inference/README.md.

2. Boot Bare-Metal Qwen3-0.6B OS in 24 KB (02-baremetal-os/)
make os FAST_Q8=1
make os-run MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin SMP=16
# Or build a bootable BIOS+UEFI ISO for QEMU / Proxmox VE:
make os-iso MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin

Full QEMU KVM, bootable ISO, and 0 GB disk Proxmox VE deployment guide: 02-baremetal-os/README.md.

3. Train Mini-GPT from Scratch in 32 KB (03-minigpt-train/)

Zero Python required to train or run inference:

mkdir -p data checkpoints && curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karpathy/char-rnn/master/data/tinyshakespeare/input.txt -o data/tinyshakespeare.txt
make train
./build/asm-gpt-train --data data/tinyshakespeare.txt --steps 400 --seq 128 -t 16 --save checkpoints/shakespeare.ckpt

Full training, live Braille TUI, checkpoint chat loop, and PyTorch gradient check guide: 03-minigpt-train/README.md.
